summary: Phase 4 testing (Service Packs + Delivery Persons + Order delivery assignment) complete. Backend: 18/18 new Phase 4 pytest cases pass (100%). Frontend: All requested data-testid elements render correctly, full happy-path e2e validated end-to-end. Tested: (1) GET /api/service-packs returns all 5 seeded packs (BASIC/PREMIUM/BRAKE/SUSP/LIGHT) with retail_price_bdt, your_price_bdt, your_tier, and bundle_items_resolved (each child has name+sku+quantity). Anonymous => retail tier (your_price_bdt == retail_price_bdt). Workshop without explicit tier => silver (5% off). Workshop with pricing_tier='gold' => your_price_bdt == retail*0.90 and your_tier='gold'. (2) Delivery persons CRUD: POST creates rider; rejects empty/whitespace name/phone with 400; GET returns list with active_assignments per rider counted from orders in {packed,shipped}; PUT updates fields; DELETE returns 200 if no active assignments and 400 if any rider has packed/shipped orders (verified by inserting an order in 'packed', confirming 400, moving to 'delivered', then 200). All endpoints correctly enforce admin auth (workshop=>403, anon=>401). (3) PATCH /api/admin/orders/{id}/delivery: assigning a rider copies name/phone/vehicle_no onto order, sets expected_delivery_date, appends a status_history entry. Setting delivery_fee_bdt updates total_bdt by delta, recomputes profit_bdt, and adjusts workshop.credit_used by the same delta when payment_method='credit' AND payment_status!='paid'. Verified deltas across 3 sequential fee changes (300 -> 500 -> 100): credit_used and total_bdt both move by +300, +200, -400 respectively. Confirmed credit_used is NOT touched for COD/non-credit orders. (4) Frontend: Workshop sidebar shows 'Service Packs' (data-testid=nav-service-packs); /service-packs renders [data-testid=packs-grid] with 5 [data-testid=pack-card-JA-PACK-*] cards and [data-testid=add-pack-*] buttons. Clicking Add Pack triggers a sonner toast 'JOY Basic Service Pack added to cart'. Admin sidebar shows 'Delivery Team' (data-testid=nav-admin-delivery); /admin/delivery-persons CRUD works through UI: 'Add Delivery Person' (data-testid=new-delivery-person-button) opens form (data-testid=delivery-person-form), Save (data-testid=save-delivery-person-button) creates a card. AdminOrderDetail shows [data-testid=delivery-card] with select/fee/date/save controls; saving assigns rider, increases admin-order-total from ৳ 5,000 to ৳ 5,250 (fee=250) and shows assigned rider info in card header. Workshop OrderDetail (/orders/:id) renders [data-testid=workshop-delivery-card] with rider name + phone + expected date.

minor.issue: No 404 when delivery_person_id is unknown — update_one silently does nothing and find_one returns null. Frontend will see null body. Should return 404.
No 404 when delivery_person_id is unknown — delete_one returns 200 with {ok:true} even if nothing was deleted.

Pydantic field delivery_fee_bdt defaults to 0.0 (not Optional[float]=None), so a request that only sends {delivery_person_id: X} is treated as fee=0.0 and will REMOVE any previously-set fee (re-applying delta = -prev_fee). To keep the fee unchanged on rider-only updates, use Optional[float]=None so the 'fee provided' branch is only entered when the client explicitly sends a fee.
Negative delivery_fee_bdt is silently ignored (the `>= 0` guard skips the branch) instead of returning 400. Should validate and reject.

bundle_items_resolved is rebuilt on every request via N+1 product lookups (one find_one per child SKU). For 5 packs * ~4 children that's ~20 round-trips per call. Consider $lookup or a single batched find.

issues: React hydration warning in console: 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>' — there's a span (probably an icon/dot) inside the native <option> in the assign-delivery-person-select. Native <option> only accepts text. Move the span outside or render label-only text inside <option>.

action_items: Fix react hydration warning on assign-delivery-person-select: do not render <span> children inside <option> in AdminOrderDetail.jsx.
Make DeliveryAssignment.delivery_fee_bdt Optional[float]=None (not 0.0 default) so rider-only saves don't accidentally zero out an existing fee.
Reject negative delivery_fee_bdt with 400 instead of silently ignoring it.
Optional perf: batch resolve bundle_items in /api/service-packs (single $in lookup instead of N+1 find_ones).

Heads-up (not in this iteration's scope but caught during regression): test_phase3 tier-pricing tests now fail because /api/orders applies tier_price() per line item (silver=5% off baked into subtotal) before the volume discount. If this is intentional, update phase3 tests to expect tier-discounted subtotals; if not, revert tier_price application in create_order. 5 phase3 tests fail this way: test_create_cod_order_success, test_order_status_progression, test_order_applies_discount_and_credit_used_post_discount, test_order_below_threshold_no_discount, test_credit_check_uses_post_discount.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1859 lines — well over the 700-line guideline. Strongly recommend splitting (auth, products, orders, admin, delivery, packs, inquiries).

DeliveryAssignment model uses fee default 0.0 instead of Optional[float]=None, so a partial PATCH (rider only) is indistinguishable from 'fee=0' and unintentionally adjusts total/credit. Use None as the sentinel.
Admin delete_delivery_person returns ok:true even when no document was deleted — should 404 to surface real errors to the UI.
Float arithmetic for money still in use (delivery_fee_bdt, credit_used $inc). At scale this drifts; recommend Decimal or paisa-as-int.
The N+1 in /api/service-packs (one find_one per bundle child) will scale poorly as packs grow. Use $lookup or aggregate({$in: child_ids}) once.
AdminOrderDetail renders <span> inside native <option> — invalid HTML and triggers React hydration warning.

rca of the issue: All Phase 4 functionality green. The single observed defect is a partial-PATCH ambiguity: when admin assigns a rider without re-entering the fee, the server treats the missing fee as 0.0 (Pydantic default) and reverses any previously-set fee. Root cause: DeliveryAssignment.delivery_fee_bdt declared as `float = 0.0` rather than `Optional[float] = None`. Mitigation: change the field type and the `if payload.delivery_fee_bdt is not None and payload.delivery_fee_bdt >= 0` guard already in place will then correctly skip updates. The current frontend always sends fee with the form, so the UI flow worked, but a future API client that sends rider-only would hit this.
